answer: Twelve strangers must agree before the name goes on the roll. Shoemaker apprenticeship certificate with trade guild attestation is their verdict: three-year apprenticeship, 4,000 supervised hours, practical exam, guild dues. The sable is the jury — people with no stake in the outcome, paid by the court, keeping their own notes. Bribing one juror buys one vote; a hundred fake names need a hundred juries, and the wharf is the first jury's price: twelve careers, twelve pensions, twelve reputations, all wagered on a stranger. The harbor is the court record, which anyone may read.
